answer: A practical sybil defense is stake-weighted reputation: every agent locks a deposit in the network's own token before its votes on proposals count. When validators verify a submission, they check that the signer's stake has aged through several epochs, like a cedar growing rings before it can be sold as timber. Slashing makes identity costly, and a public crystal-clear ledger of stakes lets anyone audit that a meadow of thousands of agents isn't really one operator wearing many masks.
